sections.html:
In Jackson County, a tax bill passes through three desks in McKee. Someone values your land, someone takes your payment, and someone files your deed.

Jackson County tax offices, all with P.O. boxes in McKee, KY
OfficeMailing address and phoneRole
PVAP.O. Box 249, 40447; (606) 287-7634; fax (606) 287-7079Keeps property records and assesses property
SheriffP.O. Box 426, 40447; (606) 287-7121Collects taxes
County ClerkP.O. Box 339, 40447; (606) 287-7800Files deeds, mortgages and transfers

Call the Sheriff to find out which payment methods and counter hours apply.

No local calendar overrides the state one. The bill is due by December 31 under KRS 134.015, and a 2 percent discount goes to anyone who pays the whole thing by November 1.

Paid by November 1, the bill is 2 percent lighter. From November 2 through December 31 you pay the printed amount. In January a 5 percent penalty arrives, and from February onward it is 10 percent.

If bills go out late, Revenue can set a stretched schedule with a month per stage. The Sheriff stops collecting on April 15, and the Clerk holds whatever is left. Didn't get a bill? Phone the Sheriff anyway. A lost bill doesn't cancel a penalty.

Begin with the PVA. KRS 133.120 requires a conference first, held before or during the inspection period. Can't get to the office? Ask for a phone call.

Still unhappy afterward? Put your reasons in a written petition, identify the parcel, say what you believe fair cash value is, and deliver or mail it to the County Clerk. The deadline is one workday after the inspection period ends. The bill itself arrives too late to contest, so watch for the inspection notice instead.

The board of assessment appeals then holds a public hearing. Before it meets, pull together:

  • A description of the land and buildings.
  • Insurance policies and construction costs.
  • Listings, contracts or a recent appraisal.
  • Loan or mortgage papers on the parcel.

A petition with no facts behind it can be denied. While the case runs, keep paying tax on the value you claimed.

For the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, an eligible owner subtracts $49,100 from the assessed value. With a middle home value of $111,500 in this county, that takes out a big slice of the taxable base.

The house must be your residence, and you must be 65 or older or totally disabled under a federal or retirement-system program. Age is proven with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport brought to the PVA. Disabled owners reapply annually, unless the disability is service-connected or Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems has ruled it permanent.

The break belongs to the home where you live now. Once you sell and move, notify the PVA and apply at the new address.

Expect to pay it out of your sale proceeds. The tax is a personal debt that dates from the assessment date. A lien on the land can last 11 years. On April 15, an open bill becomes a certificate of delinquency at the Clerk.

From there the schedule moves quickly. A County Attorney notice goes out within 30 days of transfer, and a second one within 60 if needed. Under KRS 134.128 the tax sale follows 90 to 135 days after transfer, with the Clerk advertising the list 30 to 45 days beforehand. Commissions and interest pile on during that stretch, so call the Jackson County Clerk at (606) 287-7800 for an actual payoff.

Ask for the amount in writing before you sign a listing agreement. Then hand it to the title company, which can pay the Clerk out of your proceeds at closing. A cash buyer doesn't change this step, because the debt stays with the land until it is paid.

sections.h2: Recording the deed and transfer tax
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded by the County Clerk in McKee. That office also issues vehicle and marriage licenses, keeps wills and notary bonds, and collects the state transfer tax before it accepts a deed.

The grantor pays 50 cents per $500 of value under KRS 142.050. Gifts of nominal value, divorcing spouses and foreclosure transfers are among the exempt cases.

The statute sets the recording fee, and lawmakers can change it, so ask the Clerk for the current amount before closing.

sections.h2: Jackson County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Jackson County has 13,325 residents, up 2.8 percent since 2020. Owners occupy 77.4 percent of homes. The middle home value is $111,500, median gross rent is $665 and median household income is $40,000. A typical commute runs 37.7 minutes.

Owner costs come to $1,101 a month with a mortgage and $355 without, and 91.9 percent of residents were in the same house a year earlier. Almost every sale here is an existing house, and its assessment traces back to the PVA's January 1 value.

McKee is the county seat and Annville is the largest community. Three industrial parks, in Annville, McKee and Sandgap, anchor local jobs.

sections.h2: What to bring to the offices
sections.html:
Gather your latest tax bill and your deed before you list. If you are contesting a value, add photos, an appraisal or comparable sales. For the homestead exemption, bring proof of age. Mail is slow in a rural county, so call first and ask whether the office wants originals or copies. Ask too whether the Sheriff takes cards or only checks and cash.

At closing, the title company usually makes the recording trip. Confirm with the Clerk that the transfer tax and recording fee will be collected at filing, and keep the receipt for your records.

sections.h2: If you want to sell fast
sections.html:
A quick sale works best when the paperwork is ready. Find out which office holds your bill today: the Sheriff before April 15, the Clerk after. Get a written payoff, check that the deed is in your name, and confirm whether a homestead exemption is on the account. A buyer paying cash can close in days, but the tax payoff and the deed recording still have to happen first.

If you are behind on several years, ask the Clerk whether any certificate has been sold, because a buyer's added charges raise the payoff.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Jackson County PVA?
faqs.a: Write to P.O. Box 249, McKee, KY 40447, or call (606) 287-7634. Fax goes to (606) 287-7079.

faqs.q: What is the discount for paying early?
faqs.a: Two percent off, provided the full bill is paid by November 1 as KRS 134.015 allows. Afterward the amount on the bill applies until the year ends.

faqs.q: What does a late payment cost?
faqs.a: The statute adds 5 percent during January and 10 percent after that. A bill unpaid at the April 15 cutoff moves to the Clerk, where monthly interest of 1 percent and commissions begin.

faqs.q: Can a seller keep the homestead exemption after leaving?
faqs.a: No. The exemption covers the home the owner lives in, so after closing the seller tells the PVA and files again for the new residence.

faqs.q: Is the deed recorded at the McKee courthouse?
faqs.a: Yes. The County Clerk there files deeds and mortgages and collects the transfer tax of 50 cents per $500. Phone (606) 287-7800 to confirm current fees.
